title: Dashes and Brackets for Parenthetical Clauses

atoms.b: Parenthetical clauses can sometimes be indicated by ((++brackets_or_dashes exclamation_marks)).
Brackets are used when the clause ((++does_not_contribute contributes)) to the sentence’s main idea and is ((++an_afterthought a_key_idea)), a side comment or explains circumstances.
Dashes are used when the clause ((++is is_not)) related to the sentence’s main idea and create ((++longer shorter)) pauses than commas, interrupting the sentence.

instruction.text: Why are there brackets in the following sentence?

hint.text: Careful, there may be more than one correct answer.

atoms.a: I think I saw your brother (tall, black hair, wearing glasses) at the football match.
b: ++the information is an afterthought, side comment or explains circumstances
++the information does not contribute to the sentence’s main idea
the information is related to the sentence’s main idea
the information interrupts the main sentence
atoms.sound: I think I saw your brother, tall, black hair, wearing glasses, at the football match.

instruction.text: Why are there dashes in the following sentence?

hint.text: Careful, there may be more than one correct answer.

atoms.a: He was the one - the only one - I ever truly loved.
b: the information is an afterthought, side comment, or explains circumstances
the information does not contribute to the sentence’s main idea
++the information is related to the sentence’s main idea
++the information interrupts the main sentence
atoms.sound: He was the one—the only one—I ever truly loved.

instruction.text: Why are there dashes in the following sentence?

hint.text: Careful, there may be more than one correct answer.

atoms.a: Lina - and her chipper pup, Futon - is one of our regulars at the café.
b: the information is an afterthought, side comment or explains circumstances
the information does not contribute to the sentence’s main idea
++the information is related to the sentence’s main idea
++the information interrupts the main sentence
atoms.sound: Lina—and her chipper pup Futon—is one of our regulars at the café.

instruction.text: Why are there brackets in the following sentence?

hint.text: Careful, there may be more than one correct answer.

atoms.a: They’re going to the Russian theatre (they’re learning Russian and want to practise).
b: ++the information is an afterthought, side comment or explains circumstances
++the information does not contribute to the sentence’s main idea
the information is related to the sentence’s main idea
the information interrupts the main sentence
atoms.sound: They’re going to the Russian theatre, they’re learning Russian and want to practise.

instruction.text: Why are there dashes in the following sentence?

hint.text: Careful, there may be more than one correct answer.

atoms.a: Everyone at the meeting - except the dog - said “thank you” and smiled.
b: the information is an afterthought, side comment or explains circumstances
the information does not contribute to the sentence’s main idea
++the information is related to the sentence’s main idea
++the information interrupts the main sentence
atoms.sound: Everyone at the meeting—except the dog—said 'Thank you' and smiled.
